reference: For stdin behavior, compare the candidate builtin with the independent util-linux col(1) command named by each parity case. The separate file-operand case is an explicit bash-os contract because util-linux col(1) reads stdin and rejects file operands. Builtin availability/help expectations are grounded in Bash's type/help interface and the checked-in col_doc synopsis in the documented source for column.c.
coverage: Bash builtin registration and advertised help synopsis, as metadata only.
Plain terminated input, empty input, and completion of an unterminated final line.
Default backspace preservation and -b overstrike removal.
ESC-7 and C1 reverse-index control-byte filtering plus invalid-option status compared directly.
Repeated fresh stdin redirections in one Bash process.
The documented loadable file-operand extension, checked as a contract rather than GNU parity.
Raw C1 bytes in C and decoded C1 control characters in C.UTF-8, repeated dash operands, and the custom identity banner.
exclusions: This suite does not cover every historical col control sequence, half-line motion, locale behavior, or large-input performance.
util-linux col is an stdin-only reference, so file operands are not mislabeled as parity.

cases.purpose: Check Bash reports col as a builtin and that help exposes the documented col [-b] [FILE...] synopsis; metadata is not operation coverage.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t col)
[[ $kind == builtin ]]
help_text=$(help col)
[[ $help_text == *"col [-b] [FILE...]"* ]]
printf '%s\n' "$kind"

cases.purpose: Compare ordinary newline-terminated stdin pass-through with util-linux col.
cases.script:
printf 'plain text\nsecond line\n' > input
col < input

cases.purpose: Verify empty stdin produces no output and succeeds, matching util-linux col.
Compare default-mode preservation of a backspace overstrike sequence with util-linux col.
Compare -b handling of two single-byte overstrikes with util-linux col.
Check util-linux col's output newline completion for a nonempty unterminated input stream.
cases.script:
printf 'last line without newline' > input
col -b < input

cases.purpose: Compare util-linux col's handling of an ESC-7 byte pair between lines. This checks byte output without presuming that the sequence moves output rows.
Compare handling of the C1 reverse-index byte (0x8d) embedded between printable text against util-linux col.
Compare repeated col invocations over fresh redirected stdin streams in one shell, guarding against stale persistent stdio EOF state.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha\n' > first
printf 'beta\n' > second
col -b < first
col -b < second
col -b < first

cases.purpose: Check the exit status for an unsupported option against util-linux col; report the captured command status and fail if the candidate differs.
cases.script:
: > input
rc=0
col -z < input || rc=$?
printf 'col-status=%s\n' "$rc"
test "$rc" -eq 1

cases.purpose: Check the loadable's documented FILE operand extension: two relative files form one byte stream and the nonempty unterminated final stream receives a newline. util-linux col(1) rejects file operands, so this is not GNU parity.
cases.script:
printf 'left' > first
printf 'right' > second
col -b first second

cases.purpose: Compare multiple C1 byte values in both implemented modes under the C locale.
cases.script:
printf 'A\200B\205C\215D\237E\n' > input
col < input
col -b < input

cases.purpose: Compare a valid UTF-8 C1 control codepoint adjacent to printable multibyte text.
Keep the existing bash-loadable identity banner as a custom contract, separate from external version output.
Repeated dash operands share stdin once per invocation; each fresh redirection reads the complete stream. Expected bytes follow the documented logical-stream extension.
cases.script:
printf 'A' > input
col -b - - < input
col -b - - < input
